sources.citation: Bharath Kumar, Mala Sambramalla. 2023 [degree 2024]. A Descriptive Grammar of Yerukala: An Endangered South Dravidian Language. PhD thesis, Dept. of Dravidian and Computational Linguistics, Dravidian University, Kuppam (supervisor M. C. Kesava Murty). archive.org item 20240517_20240517_1959; Shodhganga hdl 10603/549629.
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 3 Phonology (pp. 47-74) treats inventory, contrasts, distribution, clusters and syllable structure only; no stress/accent/prosody section; vowel length is called the abstractable 'supra-segmental' feature (p. 47). 'Stress' occurs only as an entry in the front-matter list of symbols. Lit. review (p. 34) merely restates Varma's 'only one suprasegmental phoneme viz. nasalisation'.

sources.citation: Sree Ramalu, G. [= G. Sreeramulu; 'Sree Ramulu' in Bharath Kumar 2023]. 2010. Yerukala samshukruthi basha sahithyamu [Yerukala culture, language and literature; in Telugu]. sources.note: Record plus one second-hand description: Shodhganga record (Dept. of Telugu, keywords Yerukala / Samshukruthi / Basha, xxi+350 pp., abstract not available); Bharath Kumar 2023 lit. review (p.36-37): Sree Ramulu's thesis 'talks about the language and their sub-groups, culture, language structure and literature of Yerukala's.. (Telugu, SKU)'. The probed bitstream (5 pp.) is an image-only scan with no text, so chapter contents were not read; whether the language-structure part says anything about accent or tone is unknown. S's guesses about Telugu-script sound lists are speculation.

sources.note: The PHOIBLE inventory derived from it (RA-1800 'Yerukala', 38 segments) lists 20 consonants and 18 vowels (incl. nasalized vowels) and no tone segments; the paper itself is a Yerukala-Tamil phonological/grammatical comparison and, like the author's 1978 book ('only one suprasegmental phoneme viz. nasalization'), is unlikely to posit tone.
